questions.solution:
The table is alphabets place value:

The pattern followed here is:                                

Sum of the positional values of the opposite alphabets letters × Total number of consonant in word = number.

LOWER → Total number of consonant (L, W, R) in the word is 3.           

Opposite alphabets of Given word is OLDVI

62 × 3 = 186

And,

MULISH → Total number of consonant (M, L, S, H) in word is 4.          

Opposite alphabets of Given word is NFORHS

Sum of the positional values of the opposite alphabets letters →

N(14) + F(6) + O(15) + R(18) + H(8) + S(19) = 14 + 6 + 15 + 18 + 8 + 19 = 80

Sum of the positional values of the opposite alphabets letters × Total number of consonant in word = number

80 × 4 = 320

Sum of the positional values of the opposite alphabets letters × Total number of consonant in word = number

questions.question: Two numbers A and B are such that the sum of 3% of A and 6% of B is four-fifths of the sum of 4% of A and 6% of B. Find the ratio of A + B and A - B.
questions.questionHtml: Two numbers A and B are such that the sum of 3% of A and 6% of B is four-fifths of the sum of 4% of A and 6% of B. Find the ratio of A + B and A - B.
questions.solution:
Given:

Sum of 3% of A and 6% of B is four-fifths of the sum of 4% of A and 6% of B

3% of A + 6% of B = 4/5 × (4% of A + 6% of B)

Both side take percent common;

=> 3 × A + 6 × B = 4/5 × (4 × A + 6 × B)

=> 5 × (3A + 6B) = 4 × (4A + 6B)

=> 15A + 30B = 16A + 24B

=> 16A – 15A = 30B – 24B

=> A = 6B

So, A : B = 6 : 1

Let common factor in A and B is x

A = 6x and B = x

Now,

A + B = 6x + x = 7x

A – B = 6x – x = 5x

The ratio of A + B and A – B is ‘7 : 5’.

Given equation 25 * 7 * 40 * 20 * 4 * 210

questions.question: The Indian Forest Act 1927 was enacted after repealing which of the following Indian forest acts?
questions.questionHtml: The Indian Forest Act 1927 was enacted after repealing which of the following Indian forest acts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Indian Forest Act, 1878.

Key Points

  • The Indian Forest Act, 1927 was enacted after repealing the Indian Forest Act, of 1878.
  • Indian Forest Act, 1927
    • The Indian Forest Act, of 1927- was enacted to consolidate the law related to forest, the transit of forest produce, and the duty liable on timber and other forests produced.
    • The preamble to the Indian Forest Act, of 1927 states that the Act seeks to consolidate the law relating to forests, the transit of forest produce and the duty that can be levied on timber and other forest produce.
    • It was largely based on previous Indian Forest Acts implemented under the British. Indian Forest Act of 1878 was the most famous one.
    • The Indian Forest Act, 1927 was enacted after repealing the Indian Forest Act, 1878 for the purpose of consolidating the law relating to forests, the transit of forest produce and the duty leviable on timber and other forest produce.
  • Indian Forest Act, 1878
    • This act repealed the Indian forest act of 1865.
    • This act was an extension of the government policy of establishing control over forests.
    • It also made several provisions for the imposition of duties on timber.
    • The basic aim of the act was to remove local rights in the reserved forest and keep them exclusively as Government reserves.
    • The 1878 act divided forests into three categories.
    1. Reserved forests. 
    2. Protected forests.
    3. Village forests. 

Additional Information

  • Indian Forest Act, 1865
    • The Indian Forest Act of 1865 extended British colonialism in India and claimed over forests in India.
    • It empowered the British government to declare any land covered with trees as a government forest and make rules to manage it.
    • It was a precursor to the Indian Forest Act of 1878.

questions.question: Which of the following plant hormones regulates growth, particularly by stimulating cell elongation in stems?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following plant hormones regulates growth, particularly by stimulating cell elongation in stems?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Auxin.

Key Points

  • Stem Elongation
    • Stem elongation refers to the rapid growth in the length of the internodes of the upper stem before the reproductive phase starts for the plant.
    • Stem elongation causes many problems for the plant, such as skinny stems that are too weak to support large flowers, as well as plants that grow too high vertically and appear spindly, so it should be prevented.
  • Auxin
    • Auxin is a group of plant hormones that regulate growth, particularly by stimulating cell elongation in stems.
    • Auxins also play a role in cell division and differentiation, in fruit development, in the formation of roots from cuttings, in the inhibition of lateral branching and in leaf fall.
    • The most important naturally occurring auxin is ß- indolyl acetic acid (IAA).

Additional Information

  • Ethylene
    • Ethylene is the first-identified plant hormone known to regulate numerous processes in plant growth, development, and response to biotic and abiotic stresses.
    • Ethylene is best known for its effect on fruit ripening and thus has great commercial importance in agriculture.
  • Gibberellin
    • Gibberellin is a group of plant hormones that occur in seeds, young leaves, and roots.
    • It stimulates the growth of main stems, especially when applied to the whole plant.
    • It is commercially obtained from fungi.
  • Cytokinin
    • Cytokinins are plant hormones that influence not only numerous aspects of plant growth, development and physiology, including cell division.
    • Cytokinins are also produced by other prokaryotic and eukaryotic organisms such as bacteria, fungi, microalgae and insects.

    • The term was first coined by a physiologist named Walter Cannon in 1926.
    • Homeostasis is the body's tendency to monitor and maintain internal states, such as temperature and blood sugar, at fairly constant and stable levels.
    • It is necessary because the body cells need to have suitable conditions around them for proper functioning.
    • The excretory system works on the principle of homeostasis in a way that all wastes or unneeded substances are removed by the body.
    • It is just like the thermostat in your house.

Additional Information

  • Consciousness
    • Consciousness is sentience or awareness of internal and external existence.
    • It refers to your individual awareness of your unique thoughts, memories, feelings, sensations, and environments.
    • Changes to consciousness can also result in changes in perception, thinking, understanding, and interpretations of the world.
  • Metabolism
    • Metabolism is the process by which your body converts what you eat and drink into energy.
    • Its purpose is the conservation of food to building blocks for proteins, lipids, nucleic acids, and some carbohydrates, and the elimination of metabolic wastes.
  • Irritability
    • It is a characteristic of living organisms in being aware of and being able to respond to a stimulus that tends to disturb the steady-state or homeostasis which all organisms prefer for maintaining life.
    • The most common scenario is distant dermatitis in a patient with a chronic eczematous leg ulcer.

questions.question: According to which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India shall a Money Bill not be introduced in a Legislative Council?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Article 198.

  • Article 198 
    • A Money Bill shall not be introduced in a Legislative Council, It can be presented in the Legislative Assembly only.
    • No money bill can be introduced in the Legislative Assembly of a State, except on the recommendations of the Governor of the state.
    • After a Money Bill has been passed by the Legislative Assembly of a State having a Legislative Council, it shall be transmitted to the Legislative Council for its recommendations, and the Legislative Council shall within a period of fourteen days from the date of its receipt of the Bill return the Bill to the Legislative.
    • Assembly with its recommendations and the Legislative Assembly may thereupon either accept or reject all or any of the recommendations of the Legislative Council.
    • If the Legislative Assembly accepts any of the recommendations of the Legislative Council, the Money Bill shall be deemed to have been passed by both Houses with the amendments recommended by the Legislative Council and accepted by the Legislative Assembly.
    • If the Legislative Assembly does not accept any of the recommendations of the Legislative Council, the Money Bill shall be deemed to have been passed by both Houses in the form in which it was passed by the Legislative Assembly without any of the amendments recommended by the Legislative Council.

Additional Information

    • Article 333 empowers the governor to nominate one Anglo-Indian to state assembly if he thinks it is not adequately represented.

Area of square = (side)2

Area of rectangle = length × breadth

The area of a square shaped field = 1764 m2

Side of square field = √1764 = 42 m

Breadth of rectangle field = (42 × 1/6) = 7 m

Cost of leveling the park = Rs. (196 × 30)

⇒ Rs. 5880

Given:

2x2 – 7x + 5

Formula used:

(a + b)3 = a3 + b3 + 3ab(a + b)

Calculation:

2x2 – 7x + 5 = 0

⇒ 2x2 + 5 = 7x

⇒ x2 + 5/2 = 7/2

⇒ x + 5/2x = 7/2

Cube of both side of equation

⇒ (x + 5/2x)3 = (7/2)3

⇒ (x)3 + (5/2x)3 + 3 × x × 5/2x(x + 5/2x) = 343/8

⇒ x3 + 125/8x3 + 15/2 (7/2) = 343/8

⇒ x3 + 125/8x3 + 105/4 = 343/8

⇒ x3 + 125/8x3 = (343/8 – 105/4)

⇒ x3 + 125/8x3 = (343 – 210)/8

⇒ x3 + 125/8x3 = 133/8

⇒ x3 + 125/8x3 = \(16\frac{5}{8}\)

∴ The required value is \(16\frac{5}{8}\)

if  \(x + {a \over bx}=G\) then \(x^3 + ({a \over bx})^3=G^3-3\times G\times {a \over b}\)

\(( {7 \over 2})^3 -3 \times {7 \over 2}\times {5 \over 2}\) 

\({7 \over 2}[( {7 \over 2})^2 -3 \times {5 \over 2}]\)

questions.question: Radha saves x% of her income. If her income increases by 28% and the expenditure increases by 20%, then her savings increase by 40%. What is the value of x ?
questions.questionHtml: Radha saves x% of her income. If her income increases by 28% and the expenditure increases by 20%, then her savings increase by 40%. What is the value of x ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Using the Alligation Method between Expenditure and Savings to find the ratio of Income components.

Expenditure increase (20%) and Savings increase (40%) result in a total Income increase (28%).

Ratio of Expenditure : Savings = (40 − 28) : (28 − 20) = 12 : 8 = 3 : 2.

Savings percentage (x) = [Savings / (Expenditure + Savings)] × 100 = [2 / (3 + 2)] × 100 = 40%.

∴ The correct answer is 40.

Alternate Method

Given: Savings = x% of Income, Income increase = 28%, Expenditure increase = 20%, Savings increase = 40%.

Formula Used: Income = Expenditure + Savings

⇒ Let Income be 100. Then Savings = x and Expenditure = 100 − x.

⇒ New Income = 100 × 1.28 = 128.

⇒ New Expenditure = (100 − x) × 1.20 = 120 − 1.2x.

⇒ New Savings = x × 1.40 = 1.4x.

⇒ New Income = New Expenditure + New Savings

⇒ 128 = (120 − 1.2x) + 1.4x

⇒ 128 − 120 = 0.2x

⇒ 8 = 0.2x

⇒ x = 8 / 0.2 = 40.

∴ The correct answer is 40.

Additional Information

Income-Expenditure Concept

The fundamental relation is Income = Expenditure + Savings. Any percentage change in components must balance this equation.

Alligation in Income Problems

When two parts of a whole change by different percentages, the overall percentage change is the weighted average. The Alligation rule helps find the initial ratio of those parts.

Successive Percentage Change

For two successive changes of a% and b%, the effective change is [a + b + (a×b)/100]%. This is useful for problems involving multiple increases/decreases.

questions.solution:
Given:

sin2 θ - cos2 θ - 3 sin θ + 2 = 0

Formula used:

cos2θ = 1 – sin2θ 

sec30° = 2/√3

tan30° = 1/√3

(sec2θ – tan2θ) = 1

Calculation:

sin2 θ – cos2 θ – 3 sin θ + 2 = 0

⇒ sin2θ – (1 – sin2θ) – 3sinθ + 2 = 0

⇒ sin2θ – 1 + sin2θ – 3sinθ + 2 = 0

⇒ 2sin2θ – 3sinθ + 1 = 0

⇒ 2sin2θ – 2sinθ – sinθ + 1 = 0

⇒ 2sinθ(sinθ – 1) – 1(sinθ – 1) = 0

⇒ (2sinθ – 1) (sinθ – 1) = 0

⇒ sinθ = 1/2, 1

⇒ sinθ = 1/2 = 30° [sin 90° = 1, we cannot take the value of 90°]

Now,

\(\frac{1}{√{\secθ-\tanθ}}\)

Multiplying with the conjugate of √secθ + tanθ 

⇒ 1/√secθ – tanθ × (√secθ + tanθ/√secθ + tanθ)

⇒ √secθ + tanθ/(sec2θ – tan2θ)

⇒ √secθ + tanθ/1

Now, put the value of θ = 30° 

⇒ √sec30° + tan30° 

⇒ √(2/√3 + 1/√3)

⇒ √(3/√3)

⇒ \(\sqrt[4]{3}\)

So, the required value is \(\sqrt[4]{3}\)

Shortcut Trick Put θ = 30° 

⇒ sin230° - cos230° - 3 sin30° + 2

⇒ (1/4) - (3/4) - (3/2) + 2

⇒ (-1/2) - (3/2) + 2

⇒ - 2 + 2 = 0

Now,

\(\frac{1}{√{\secθ-\tanθ}}\)

Multiplying with the conjugate of √secθ + tanθ 

⇒ 1/√secθ – tanθ × (√secθ + tanθ/√secθ + tanθ)

⇒ √secθ + tanθ/(sec2θ – tan2θ)

⇒ √secθ + tanθ/1

Now, put the value of θ = 30° 

⇒ √sec30° + tan30° 

⇒ √(2/√3 + 1/√3)

⇒ √(3/√3)

⇒ \(\sqrt[4]{3}\)

So, the required value is \(\sqrt[4]{3}\)

(a + b)2 = a2 + b2 + 2ab

(a – b)2 = a2 + b2 – 2ab

According to the question

Squaring both sides, we get

Vertices A, B,C and D of a quadrilateral ABCD lie on a circle

Concept used:

We know that in cyclic quadrilateral the sum of opposite angle is 180°.

Calculation:

⇒ ∠A + ∠C = 180° 

⇒ 3θ + θ = 180° 

⇒ 4θ = 180° 

⇒ θ = 45° 

⇒ ∠C = 45° 

Again,

⇒ ∠B + ∠D = 180° 

⇒ α + 2α = 180° 

⇒ 3α = 180° 

⇒ α = 60° 

⇒ ∠B = 60° 

The value of ∠D = 2α = (2 × 60) = 120° 

The difference between the measures of ∠D and ∠C = (120° – 45°)

⇒ 75°

⇒ 75°

questions.question: In an examination, the average score of a student was 67.6. If he would have got 27 more marks in Mathematics, 10 more marks in Computer Science, 18 more marks in History and retained the same marks in other subjects, then his average score would have been 72.6. How many papers were there in the examination?
questions.questionHtml: In an examination, the average score of a student was 67.6. If he would have got 27 more marks in Mathematics, 10 more marks in Computer Science, 18 more marks in History and retained the same marks in other subjects, then his average score would have been 72.6. How many papers were there in the examination?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Increase in Total Marks = 27 + 10 + 18 = 55

Increase in Average Score = 72.6 − 67.6 = 5

Number of papers = Total Marks Increase ÷ Average Increase

Number of papers = 55 ÷ 5 = 11

∴ The correct answer is 11.

Alternate Method

Given: Initial average = 67.6, Final average = 72.6, Mathematics increase = 27, Computer Science increase = 10, History increase = 18.

Formula Used: Total Marks = Average × Number of Papers

⇒ Let the total number of papers be n.

⇒ Total initial marks = 67.6 × n

⇒ Total marks added = 27 + 10 + 18 = 55

⇒ New total marks = 67.6n + 55

⇒ New average = (67.6n + 55) ÷ n = 72.6

⇒ 67.6n + 55 = 72.6n

⇒ 72.6n − 67.6n = 55

⇒ 5n = 55

⇒ n = 11

∴ The correct answer is 11.

Additional Information

Definition of Average

Average (Mean) is the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations. Formula: Avg = Σx ÷ n.

Effect of Constant Addition

If every observation in a set is increased by a constant value k, the new average also increases by k.

Deviation Method

The sum of deviations of all observations from their mean is always zero. This concept is useful in finding missing values or balancing averages.

questions.question: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 12 hours and 16 hours respectively and pipe C can empty the full tank in 24 hours. All three pipes are opened together, but after 4 hours pipe B is closed. In how many hours, the empty tank will be completely filled?
questions.questionHtml: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 12 hours and 16 hours respectively and pipe C can empty the full tank in 24 hours. All three pipes are opened together, but after 4 hours pipe B is closed. In how many hours, the empty tank will be completely filled?
questions.solution:
Given:

Time taken to fill a tank by Pipe A = 12 hours

Time taken to fill a tank by Pipe B = 16 hours

Time taken to empty a tank by Pipe C = 24 hours

Formula used:

Work = Efficiency × Time

Calculation:

LCM of 12, 16 and 24 is 48

Efficiency of A to fill the tank = (48/12) = 4 hours/day

Efficiency of B to fill the tank = (48/16) = 3 hours/day

Efficiency of C to empty the tank = (48/24) = - 2 hours/day

All three pipes opened together for 4 hours = [(4 + 3 – 2) × 4]

⇒ (5 × 4) = 20 unit

Remaining unit = (48 – 20) = 28 unit

Time taken by A and C together = [28/(4 – 2)]

⇒ (28/2) = 14 hours

Now,

Total time is taken to fill the empty tank = (14 + 4) hours

⇒ 18 hours

∴ The required time is 18 hours

Shortcut Trick

Effective efficiency = 5

In 4 hours all three pipes will fill 5 × 4 = 20 units

Now, Remaining 48 - 20 = 28 units will be filled by A and C

So, Total efficiency of A and C = 2

So, time = 28/2 = 14 hours

Total time = 14 + 4 = 18 hours

Divisibility rule of 7 - If a number is divisible by 7, then the difference between twice the unit digit of the given number and the remaining part of the given number should be a multiple of 7 or it should be equal to 0

questions.question: In triangle ABC, AD is the bisector of ∠A. If AB = 5 cm, AC = 7.5 cm and BC = 10 cm, then what is the distance of D from the mid-point of BC (in cm)?
questions.questionHtml: In triangle ABC, AD is the bisector of ∠A. If AB = 5 cm, AC = 7.5 cm and BC = 10 cm, then what is the distance of D from the mid-point of BC (in cm)?
questions.solution:
Given:

AB = 5 cm

AC = 7.5 cm

BC = 10 cm

Concept used:

Angle bisector theorem:  The angle bisector of a triangle bisects the opposite side in such a way that the ratio of the two-line segments is proportional to the ratio of the other two sides.

Midpoint theorem: The line segment in a triangle joining the midpoint of two sides of the triangle is said to be parallel to its third side and is also half of the length of the third side.

Calculation:

AD is the bisector of ∠A

⇒ AB/AC = BD/DC  [By angle bisector theorem]

⇒ 5/7.5 = BD/DC

⇒ 2/3 = BD/DC

3/2 = DC/BD

Adding 1 to both sides, we get:

\(\frac{3}{2}\) + 1 = \(\frac{DC}{BD}\) + 1

\(\frac{5}{2}\) = \(\frac{BD+DC}{BD}\) = \(\frac{BC}{BD}\)

Since BC = 10, we get:

The value of BD = (2/5 × 10) = 4

The value of DC = (3/5 × 10) = 6

According to the question

Midpoint of BC = (10/2) = 5

So, We take, M as a midpoint on BC = 5

Now,

The distance between D and M = (6 – 5) = 1

So, the required value is 1 cm

questions.questionHtml: A boat covers a round trip journey between two points A and B in a river in T hours. If its speed in still water becomes 2 times, it would take \(\frac{80}{161}\) T hours for the same journey. Find the ratio of its speed in still water to the speed of the river.
questions.solution:
Given: 

A boat covers a round trip journey between two points A and B in a river in T hours

Formula used:

Downstream = (u + v) km/hr

Upstream = (u – v) km/hr

Calculation:

Let the speed of boat in still water be xkm/hr

Speed of stream = y km/hr

Let the distance between them be d 

Downstream = (x + y) km/hr

Upstream = (x – y) km/hr

According to the question

⇒ d/(x + y) + d/(x – y) = 161T

⇒ d(x - y + x + y)/ x2 - y2 = 161T

⇒d(2x)/161(x2 - y2) = T   ......... (1)

Again,

⇒ d/(2x + y) + d/(2x – y) = 80T

⇒d(2x - y + 2x + y)/(2x)2 - (y)2 = 80T

⇒d(4x) / 80(4x2 - y2) = T  ..........(2)

Now equalling both the equations,

⇒d(2x)/161(x2 - y2) = d(4x) / 80(4x2 - y2) 

⇒1/161(x2 - y2) = 2/ 80(4x2 - y2) 

⇒1/(161x2 - 161y2) = 1/(160x2 - 40y2)

⇒160x2 - 40y2 = 161x2 - 161y2

⇒x2 = 121y2

⇒x/y = 11/1

∴ The required ratio is 11 : 1

Alternate Method 

Let the speed of boat in still water be xkm/hr

Speed of stream = y km/hr

Let the distance between them be d 

Downstream = (x + y) km/hr

Upstream = (x – y) km/hr

According to the question

⇒ d/(x + y) + d/(x – y) = T

⇒ d(1/x + y) + (1/x – y) = T

⇒ d[(x – y) + (x + y)/(x2 – y2)] = T

⇒ d[(2x/(x2 – y2) = T

⇒ d/T = x2 – y2/2x .....(1)

Again,

⇒ d/(2x + y) + d/(2x – y) = 80T/161

⇒ d(1/2x + y + 1/2x – y) = 80T/161

⇒ d(2x – y+ 2x + y)/4x2 – y2 = 80T/161

⇒ d(4x/4x2 – y2) = 80T/161

⇒ d/T = 80(4x2 – y2)/4x × 161 ......(2)

Now, substituting both the equation, we get

d/T = x2 – y2/2x =  80(4x2 – y2)/4x × 161

⇒ x2 – y2 = 40(4x2 – y2)/161

⇒ (161x2 – 161y2) = (160x2 – 40y2)

⇒ (161x2 – 160x2) = (161y2 – 40y2)

⇒ x2 = 121y2

⇒ x/y = 11/1

∴ The required ratio is 11 : 1

In this type of question, always try to make two equations equal to the same variable so that we can equalize the two equations.
